subject: Flexible commit bucket + grace period — Starlane renewal discussion
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@starlane.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Flexible commit bucket + grace period — Starlane renewal discussion

Hi Laura —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Per our conversation I put together a short proposal to help Starlane bridge the seasonal spike you saw in Q2 while keeping your unit economics predictable through the renewal. High level:

- 12-month renewal with a flexible commit bucket: base commit + a 20% burst buffer for the first 3 months.
- 60-day grace period for true-ups (we'll allow overages to be reconciled without immediate late charges during that window).
- One-time retroactive credit to offset the Q2 spike (proposal: $25,000 applied to the first invoice).
- Temporary price hold for any model variants included in the commit for the first 6 months.

I attached a draft addendum (Proposed_Addendum_v1.pdf) that shows how this sits in the order form and the invoices. If you're comfortable with the approach, we can:
1) circulate an operational addendum to procurement/legal,
2) run the internal approval for the one-time credit, and
3) route the finalized addendum to DocuSign.

Questions for you: is the 20% burst buffer the right size for the expected seasonal uplift? Do you need a longer/richer true-up window?

If helpful, Vanessa can run an expected spend projection against the commit to show how the credit and burst buffer interact.

Thanks — happy to hop on one more quick call today.

Best,
Sean
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: Proposed_Addendum_v1.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@starlane.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@starlane.com>; Legal <legal@starlane.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Flexible commit bucket + grace period — Starlane renewal discussion

Sean —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the thoughtful structure. A few notes from our side after reviewing with ops and finance:

- The burst buffer looks reasonable but we were hoping for 30% for the first 2 months and 10% thereafter (our peak is early July). Can you accommodate that split?
- 60 days for true-ups is helpful — would you consider waiving any reconciliation charges if we materially exceed commit due to a confirmed customer contract we have in the pipeline (we can provide evidence)?
- The retroactive credit is important; $25k is a good start but can we split it into $15k applied to invoice 1 and $10k as a service credit usable for overage in the year (to be applied automatically)?

I've attached our Q2 usage export for your finance/ops team to check the numbers. If we can get to agreement on the structure, procurement prefers a single addendum and one DocuSign envelope.

Laura Chen
Head of Platform Ops, Starlane Logistics
laura.chen@starlane.com
Attachment: usage_report_q2.csv (CSV, 12KB)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Flexible commit bucket + grace period — Starlane renewal discussion

Team — forwarding Laura's reply and Q2 export. Short ask: can we approve the following concessions to close this renewal this week?

Proposed concessions (summary):
- Burst buffer: 30% for months 1-2, 10% for month 3 (effectively a weighted 23% over first 3 months).
- Grace period: remain 60 days, and waive reconciliation fees if Starlane provides a signed customer contract showing the additional usage (will require ops verification).
- Retroactive credit: split $15k to invoice 1 + $10k service credit applied to overage during the 12-month term.
- Price hold: 6 months on the model bundle in the commit.

Impact/notes:
- I ran rough math (attached internal_calculation.xlsx) — cost to Redwood for the retro credit + burst is roughly $18-22k if they use the full burst; with the price hold the ongoing unit economics are protected for them.
- This is a strategic account: expansion potential with a logistics partner upstream (two-year ARR motion).
- Procurement wants a single addendum and a DocuSign flow.

Need approvals: 
- Marissa: approve commercial terms (credit + burst buffer structure)
- Neha: approve finance treatment and sign-off on applying $15k to invoice vs service credit.
- Vanessa: ops to confirm we can auto-apply the $10k service credit to overages in billing system and verify the process for evidence-based fee waiving.

Thanks — if you can reply with quick thumbs (or one-line approval) I'll include in the DocuSign-ready addendum.

Sean

Attachment: internal_calculation.xlsx (XLSX, 34KB)

Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Flexible commit bucket + grace period — Starlane renewal discussion

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the clear asks and for sharing the Q2 export. We've reviewed internally and can confirm the following approved terms:

1) Burst buffer: 30% for months 1-2, 10% for month 3 (operationalized as an auto-burst with priority routing until burst pool exhausted).
2) Grace period: 60 days true-up window. Reconciliation fees will be waived if Starlane provides a verifiable customer contract for usage above commit within 30 days of the overage event. Redwood ops will perform verification.
3) Retroactive credit: $15,000 applied to the first post-renewal invoice; $10,000 issued as a service credit to be applied automatically to any overage during the 12-month term.
4) Price hold: 6 months on the included model bundle.

Next steps:
- I'll upload a final addendum (Starlane_Renewal_Addendum_v2.docx) to the drive and route a single DocuSign envelope to procurement/legal.
- Vanessa, please follow up on the auto-credit workflow and confirm execution steps in the implementation thread.
- Neha, I copy you for billing treatment confirmation.

Laura — if that matches what you need, we will send the DocuSign today and aim for effective renewal on 2027-07-01 to cover the July peak.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com
+1 (650) 555-0147

Attachment: Starlane_Renewal_Addendum_v2.docx (DOCX, 102KB)
